newsitem.title: INDIA: FOCUS-India's STC boosts wheat import commitments.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-India's STC boosts wheat import commitments.

text.p: India's state-run State Trading Corp (STC) said on Friday it had contracted to import 2.74 million tonnes of wheat since December 1996.
"We have firmed up (import) contracts for a total of 2.74 million tonnes of wheat (since December 1996)," STC chairman B.K. Chaturvedi told reporters in the Indian capital.
He said STC contracted to import 1.74 million tonnes in 1996/97 (April-March).
"We have firmed up contracts for one million tonne more. This was done in the last week of March," Chaturvedi said.
He said the additional one million tonne had been bought from Australia for arrival from August 1997 onwards.
Chaturvedi said of the previously contracted 1.74 million tonnes wheat, one million had arrived by March 31 and the rest was expected by May.

Asked whether the government had authorised the import of the one million tonnes in addition to the two million tonnes already authorised in December 1996, Chaturvedi said, "Whatever has been done is under government authorisation."
Earlier on Friday an STC official said the company had contracted to import only 1.74 million tonnes since December 1996.
Chaturvedi said of the total imports, nearly 2.3 million tonnes had been purchased from Australia.
The total cost of wheat imports is expected to be around 1.5 billion rupees.
India banned exports of wheat in September 1996 when stock limits fell to very low levels due to four million tonnes less procurement by state agencies than estimated.

Food Minister Devendra Prasad Yadav told parliament in March that India's wheat stocks on April 1 were projected at 2.72 million tonnes, down one million from the buffer stock norms of 3.7 million tonnes set by the government.
In December India authorised the state-run State Trading Corporation (STC) to import two million tonnes of wheat to build stocks and check rising prices.
The Agriculture Ministry has put the 1996/97 (July-June) wheat crop at 64.5 million tonnes against 62.6 million in 1995/96.
Chaturvedi said STC exported about 150,000 tonnes of soymeal valued at two billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March), mainly to China, Indonesia and Phillipines.
STC said in a statement its net profit doubled to 440 million rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) from 220 million in 1995/96.
Its turnover increased to 23.17 billion rupees in 1996/97 from 16.85 billion in the previous year.
STC had set a turnover target of 28.90 billion rupees for 1997/98, the statement added.
